rounds.text: Longspur International Ventures Ltd carries significant valuation and fundamental risks that are unsupported by the evidence. The business trades at an exorbitant P/E of 494.92x against a sector benchmark of 20.19x, alongside an EV/EBITDA of 279.68x that massively dwarfs the sector benchmark of 14x [E6, E11]. Compounded share price growth has been negative over the medium term, declining by 4% over three years and 21% over one year, with the stock currently sitting only 23% of the way up its 52-week range [E5, E18, E19]. Valuation models highlight a stark disconnect, as a discounted cash flow model puts intrinsic value at Rs 4 per share against a market price of Rs 6.65, resulting in a severe margin of safety of -70.8% [E29, E30]. Fundamentally, the company generates low returns with an ROE of 4.6% and ROCE of 6.9%, while its current ratio of 0.81x indicates that current liabilities exceed current assets [E12, E13, E24]. Furthermore, net profit plummeted -58% YoY, and the rules-based screen scores a modest 43 out of 100 with a neutral, medium confidence rating [E38, E41]. Conceded: [E14], [E15].

While the bear points to elevated P/E and EV/EBITDA multiples, the market capitalisation sits at a modest ₹ 20.5 Cr [E3, E6, E11] and the stock trades at just 0.41x book value on a price of ₹ 6.65 against a book value of ₹ 16.1 [E2]. The historical share price decline and position at 23% of the 52-week range ignore the company's surging fundamentals, specifically a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 118% and profit growth of 143% [E5, E14, E15, E18, E19]. Regarding valuation models, profit growth is actively starting to outperform expectations, with recent profit growth exceeding 1-year price growth by 164% [E33]. The company operates with a conservatively financed debt-to-equity ratio of 0.02x and is flagged as almost debt-free, which substantially mitigates balance sheet concerns [E23, E35]. Furthermore, the company's ROA of 4.42% outperforms the sector benchmark of 1.93%, and its ROCE of 6.92% exceeds the sector median of 6.1% [E8, E10, E48]. Conceded: [E24], [E29], [E30], [E41].

The bull’s reliance on a low price-to-book ratio of 0.41x [E2, E36] ignores the reality that the market is pricing the company at a massive premium relative to its actual earnings power, with a P/E of 494.92x compared to a sector benchmark of 20.19x [E6]. While the bull highlights recent growth [E14, E15], these figures are contradicted by a reported net profit decline of 58% year-over-year [E41] and an inconsistent operating margin trend [E21]. The claim that the company is safely financed is undermined by a current ratio of 0.81x, indicating that current liabilities exceed current assets [E24], and the emergence of debt where there was none previously [E25]. Furthermore, the bull’s optimism regarding valuation is directly refuted by a discounted cash flow analysis that suggests the stock is overvalued by 70.8% [E29, E30, E43]. Conceded: [E3, E8, E10, E23, E35, E48]. The stock’s poor performance, evidenced by a 21% decline over the last year and a 4% decline over three years, suggests that the market has already factored in the risks that the bull chooses to overlook [E18, E19].
